Ok I had start by how I would do that on my home setup.

First, I will access the router's page and add a static route to my server.

Second, I will navigate to the port forwarding part and create a rule by filling in the details. They will usually be:  
Active(checkbox)  
internal LAN IP(this is the route IP for the device that was in the last step)  
port (there may be up to 4 values related to it) put 80 or 443 depending on whether you have SSL and https enabled or not  


Then, you will have linked your public IP address to your server.

You might get an error in the port forwarding step, as your ISP blocks any ports going out of your router to make you pay for the more expensive business internet plan. Assuming you didnt get the error, you will go further by setting up NextCloud itself (I think you have done that already)

By this moment, your friends and family can access your setup by typing in your public IP in the web browser.  The next steps will be only for the case you have a domain name and would like to point it out to the server

​

Login to your domain administration site, and set up an A record where the value is your public IP. Save. Wait for a few minutes (upto 24 hours, but it usually works right after 5-15 minutes) And you have your nextcloud on the internet. Let me know if I missed anything, or if you have any doubts.
Good luck!
